topic.title: ₹85,000 crore gone! PB Fintech to HDFC Bank — these 5 financial stocks witness highest wealth erosion on IRDAI's move
topic.source_snippet: Financial stocks faced significant selloff on Thursday due to proposed changes by IRDAI to insurance distribution and commission structures, erasing  ₹1.12 lakh crore in market capitalisation. Major losses were seen in Bajaj Finance, PB Fintech, HDFC Bank, and Axis Bank, leading the decline.

slides.headline: The Hidden Risk Behind ₹85,000 Crore Gone

comparison_data.myth: Retail belief: Sudden drops on major stocks like PB Fintech and HDFC Bank create an instant dip-buying discount.
comparison_data.reality: Institutional truth: ₹1.12 lakh crore wiped out via systemic distribution, trapping late retail buyers in falling knives.

slides.title: The Brutal Cost of Chasing Headlines

stat_data.label: wealth erosion in financial stocks
stat_data.context: Proposed IRDAI commission changes triggered massive institutional block deals. Retail portfolios suffered severe compounding losses while chasing perceived value.

flowchart_data.text: Regulatory draft release triggers automated algorithmic selling by institutional desks.
Smart money executes block distribution while retail absorbs the falling liquidity.
Price discovery bottoms out only after retail capital is entirely exhausted.

slides.title: The Mathematical Drag Of Panic Selling
slides.card_text: When policy shifts threaten distribution margins, institutional portfolios rebalance instantly. Retail capital lacks structural speed, absorbing the downward slippage and funding institutional block exits at peak volatility.

slides.title: The Non-Negotiable Execution Rule
slides.card_text: Never chase a headline move without verifying volume distribution and delivery percentages. Structural regulatory shocks require waiting for institutional accumulation phases to complete before deploying capital.
